newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end weaker, electricity stocks slump.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end weaker, electricity stocks slump.

text.p: Chilean shares ended softer for the second day as foreign investors cashed in gains from the recent rally in electricity shares, said dealers.
"The market adjusted upward and now profit-takers have moved in," said Lance Eckel, an analyst at brokerage Sud Americano. "People are waiting for results and sniffing around for bargains."
The selective index is likely to hover around 115 points in coming sessions, he said. The IPSA index ended down 1.23 percent at 114.28 points. The general index lost 0.67 percent to 5,281.31 points.
Turnover shrank to 13.8 billion pesos from 20 billion pesos Monday.
Electricity shares, which had risen sharply last week, retreated on profit-taking and fears about the impact on earnings of this year's drought, said dealers.
"There are jitters about the drought as there's no end in sight," said one trader.
Investors reacted negatively to a media report that the government is worried about the rise in power consumption in recent months, they said.
The market fears electricity may have to rationed if demand continues to rise as the drought has hurt hydro-electric generators power output.
Enersis lost 2.03 percent to 266 pesos, while Endesa shed 1.85 percent to 251-3/4 pesos.
Winners included power utility Chilquinta, up 1.26 percent at 1,975 pesos, glass-maker Cristales, up 0.89 percent at 2,840 pesos and forestry firm Masisa, which rose 0.44 percent to 227 pesos.
